items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: And Stanley brought him around to meet everybody.

ctx.x: I think he was sixteen. Now, I think he was sixteen... But anyway, he was very young, and that's when he first came out. And Stanley brought him around to meet everybody. And we'd hang out in Stanley's place lots of nights, you know, because he had a small, intimate kind of place. And this is where I heard some classic works.

You probably remember the recording that Charlie Parker made on "Lover Man." Well, I knew what inspired that particular recording. One night we were all in the Casablanca, and he played "Lover Man," and he played so great on "Lover Man" until when he finished his chorus, no other horn player put a horn to his mouth. And the time just kept going on... And he looked up and smiled, and put his horn back in his mouth and kept on playing, you know. It was classic. It was classic, you know. Nobody had to play. Oh, I…
